_comment: The declared identity of the instrument on this branch. CI recomputes the
source, model-facing and outcome-facing identities from the working tree
and fails when any differs from the values below, so a behavioural or
grading change cannot land without somebody editing this file deliberately.
This file is deliberately OUTSIDE the hashed surface. It sits at the
repository root, and provenance._HASHED_FILES contains only pyproject.toml,
so editing it does not move the number it declares. If it were hashed, every
Generation 2 has no collected dataset yet. outcome_contract_sha256 was
introduced while generation 2 was still being prepared, so declaring the
existing generation-2 outcome contract here does not create a generation-3
boundary. The first generation-2 model row must match all three identities.
how_to_recompute: python -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); from local_agent import provenance as p; print(p.source_sha256()); print(p.base_prompt_sha256()); print(p.outcome_contract_sha256())"
when_this_changes: source_sha256 moves for any change to hashed source. Update this file in
the same commit. A source-only move does not automatically end a generation;
whether archived rows can be re-scored is decided from the evidence they
base_prompt_sha256 moves when the model-facing contract changes: what the
model sees or the submission contract it must satisfy.
outcome_contract_sha256 moves when the outcome-facing contract changes:
task contracts, oracle semantics, or the evaluator logic that decides what
Either contract-axis move ENDS A GENERATION once rows exist under the current
generation. Increment 'generation', preserve the previous identities, and
record the boundary in docs/experiment-design.md. Confirmatory data does not
cross that boundary. Archived evidence may still support explicitly versioned
re-scoring when measurement/rescore_dataset.py can do so without guessing.
